science.title: A genome-wide association study based on plasma high-throughput untargeted metabolomic profiles expands the number of genetically influenced metabolites in pigs
science.description: Metabolomics is a powerful phenomics approach for investigating the molecular mechanisms linking genotype to phenotype and identifying biologically informative traits for precision livestock breeding. However, the genetic architecture of the plasma metabolome remains incompletely characterised in pigs. Here, we investigated the genetic determinism of plasma metabolites in 268 Italian Duroc pigs using untargeted high-throughput metabolomics and genome-wide association analyses. Plasma metabolomic analysis identified 580 quality-controlled metabolites, which were integrated with genotypes from a panel of approximately 60,000 single nucleotide polymorphisms. Heritability estimates indicated moderate genetic contribution on the plasma metabolome, with ~ 46% of metabolites showing heritability greater than 0.20. Overall, 89 metabolite quantitative trait loci (mQTL) regions were identified, involving 156 metabolites and metabolite ratios. Most associations were related to lipid and amino acid metabolism, and several loci harboured biologically plausible candidate genes involved in transport, enzymatic activity, and metabolic regulation. Several mQTL exhibited pleiotropic effects, some metabolites showed evidence of polygenic control, and conditional and ratio-based analyses uncovered additional associations not detected by single-metabolite analyses alone. These findings improve the biological interpretation of metabolic pathways underlying economically relevant traits and support the integration of metabolomics and genomics for precision breeding, feeding, and management strategies in pigs.

science.title: Role of lactylation-related genes in heatstroke-induced ventricular arrhythmias by integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analysis and experimental validation
science.description: Heatstroke (HS) is associated with cardiac injury and ventricular arrhythmias (VAs). Although high lactate levels are common in HS, their association with HS-induced VAs requires investigation. We established a rat HS model using a 42 °C core body temperature endpoint. Hemodynamics and inflammation were evaluated using pressure–volume (PV) loops and immunofluorescence validation of selected targets. Electrophysiological properties were assessed via in vivo telemetry, programmed electrical stimulation, and optical mapping. Furthermore, we performed integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses to identify molecular alterations. HS rats exhibited impaired hemodynamics and macrophage infiltration. Electrophysiological tests showed higher VA inducibility, slowed ventricular conduction, and calcium transient alternans. In the myocardium, Cx43 displayed structural disorganization and increased phosphorylation, and both lactate levels and global protein lactylation increased. Multi-omics analyses showed that the mRNA levels of Hspa1a, Sirt1, and Crebbp increased. However, only the HSPA1A protein increased, whereas the SIRT1 and CREBBP protein levels decreased. HS-induced cardiac injury and VAs are accompanied by impaired hemodynamics, Cx43 alterations, and increased protein lactylation. These phenotypic changes coincide with differences between the mRNA and protein levels of SIRT1 and CREBBP, which are potentially associated with VAs during HS.

science.title: Biphasic bacterial physiological response to plasma-activated water revealed by nanomotion sensing
science.description: Plasma-activated water (PAW) is widely studied for its antimicrobial properties, yet bacterial responses to sub-lethal concentrations remain poorly characterized and understood. Here, we quantitatively investigate bacterial physiological responses to PAW under nutrient-rich conditions using colony-forming unit (CFU) counting and nanomotion sensing. CFU measurements reveal complete bacterial inactivation at high PAW concentrations, confirming its strong antimicrobial activity. However, intermediate concentrations induce increased bacterial proliferation compared to nutrient-matched controls, indicating enhanced physiological activity under sub-lethal exposure. Nanomotion sensing independently confirms this biphasic response, showing increased oscillatory activity at intermediate concentrations and complete signal suppression at bactericidal levels. These measurements provide real-time, single-cell evidence of concentration-dependent physiological modulation. The observed response is consistent with adaptive activation under moderate reactive species exposure and inactivation at higher concentrations. These findings quantitatively demonstrate that bacterial interactions with PAW are not limited to monotonic inhibition but involve a broader physiological response landscape. These results further demonstrate that nanomotion sensing can rapidly quantify antimicrobial thresholds and detect subtle physiological responses to plasma-derived reactive species. This provide new insights into microbial responses to PAW, and may help optimizing plasma-based antimicrobial applications.

science.title: Identification of thermal sensitizers that enhance heat stress-induced apoptosis
science.description: Hyperthermia has emerged as a therapeutic approach for cancer treatment by inducing apoptotic cell death through exposure to elevated temperatures. Nevertheless, the antitumor efficacy of hyperthermia is frequently compromised by variations in tumor characteristics and adaptive cellular responses that promote thermotolerance. To improve therapeutic outcomes, hyperthermia has been combined with thermal sensitizers, such as chemotherapeutic drugs, capable of increasing cellular sensitivity to heat stress. In our previous study, SB366791, an inhibitor of heat stress-induced scaffold attachment factor B granule formation, promoted apoptosis under heat stress conditions; however, its ability to induce apoptosis was limited. Therefore, we conducted a chemical library screening to identify more potent thermal sensitizers that could augment heat stress-mediated apoptosis. Six candidate compounds were identified as enhancers of heat-induced apoptosis in HeLa cells. Notably, these compounds exhibited greater pro-apoptotic effects under heat stress conditions than 5-fluorouracil. In addition, under normal conditions, Z134808806, Z228922334, Z198049864, and Z318719814 caused cell cycle arrest at the G1 phase, whereas Z134809032 induced G2/M phase arrest. Collectively, these findings suggest that the identified compounds may serve as effective thermal sensitizers and provide potential candidates for improving hyperthermia-based anticancer strategies.
